LESSON: OUR RIGHTS AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade two
Subject: ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES
Strand: Social environment
Topic 1.5: Our Rights and Responsibilities
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 6

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Our Rights and Responsibilities, part of Social environment in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade two ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: Why are child rights and responsibilities important at school?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Our Rights and Responsibilities together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and Collaboration: Teamwork is developed as learners role play responsibilities of children in school.

● Digital Literacy: Learners interact with digital technology as they use digital devices to explore responsibilities of children in school.

● Citizenship: Active community/family life skill is developed as learners share their experiences on child rights and responsibilities using

age-appropriate stories.

Values:
● Social justice: Learners enhance equity as they perform age-appropriate responsibilities at school.

● Respect: Learners enhance human dignity when they share their experiences on Child Rights using age-appropriate stories.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
● Child care protection: Learners develop child rights awareness as they share their experiences on child rights and responsibilities using

age-appropriate stories.

● Link to other Learning Areas:

● Languages: Child Rights and responsibilities stories can be used when learners actively engage in listening/observing and

speaking/signing skills.

Suggested learning resources

Approved learning support materials ,Flash cards ,Pictures ,DLP devices,
